issuer.summary: Pro rata vault claim with cash-limited queued exits. Enforcement sits with the relevant loan agent or lender. Loan-specific protection and historic procedures provide limited assurance. November 18 NIM allocation proposal remained in active Snapshot voting at review.
issuer.summary_source: DeFiAnalyst exact Arbitrum component review, November 27. Issuer 5.0 remains provisional. Documentary observation only.
facts: sUSDai represents a pro rata vault position. The vault benefits from loan payments through Depositor NFTs. GPU Finance Ltd. may act as agent or lender of record, with alternative agents possible. Wilmington Trust’s disclosed escrow role is loan-specific. Holders have no documented individual enforcement right, secured ranking or guaranteed exit. The product page describes cash-constrained FIFO processing in global 30-day epochs, partial fills and carryover. Operational QEV auctions remain unverified.

Risk docs describe a DSRA of about 1–3 months of peak debt service. CHIP staking has no current protocol function. Barkr protection applies to qualifying server sales, excludes whole-SPV sales and can be suspended during market-wide shocks. Current portfolio-wide first-loss capacity and direct policy rights remain unverified. The latest linked TNF report covers specified loan procedures at July 15, issued August 25. It gives no current reserve, recovery, solvency or redemption opinion.

The November 18 CRFC proposes allocating the protocol share of sUSDai NIM after Foundation expenses to CHIP purchases from January 1, 2027. The Snapshot vote was active at review. No executed allocation, new holder guarantee or available first-loss capital established.

On November 23 USD.AI announced Tony Giacin as Head of Capital Markets and Hani Abdul Baki as Head of Originations. The announcement identifies operating personnel and supplies no transfer of token obligations or deployed administrative authority.
